description: Orpheus descends to the Underworld to bring back Eurydice. His music bends death. A single forbidden look is enough to lose everything.

hero.hook: His lyre soothes the Underworld. Her doubt makes Eurydice forever.

blocks.text: **Orpheus** is a musician whose lyre even moves stones. When his wife **Eurydice** dies, he refuses to mourn. He goes down alive to the dead to bring her back.
The Latin poets  and  fixed this story. Beyond tragic love, it is a story about doubt, impatience and the power of art in the face of death. [[Virgil]] [[Ovid]]

Orpheus is son of the Muse **Calliope**. His **lyre**, gift from **Apollo**, god of the arts, is not only used to please. She calms animals, moves trees, calms wild nature. Where other heroes win by force, Orpheus triumphs by harmony.

blocks.caption: Orpheus and his lyre: art as power over the world.

blocks.text: During the expedition of the **Argonauts**, led by the hero , the Sirens try to attract the crew. Orpheus sings louder and saves his companions. Then he marries the dryad **Eurydice**, a wood nymph. Happiness is brief. [[Jason]]
On the wedding day, Eurydice flees the shepherd . She steps on a snake. The venom kills her. His shadow leaves towards the , river of Hell. [[Aristaeus]] [[Styx]]

Orpheus attempts a : a descent into Hell. No weapons. Only his music. She puts , the three-headed dog who guards the entrance, to sleep. She flexes , the boatman of the dead. [[Catabasis]] [[Cerberus]] [[Charon]]

In front of **Hadès** and **Persephone**, sovereigns of the underworld, Orpheus plays the most moving tune of his life. The Underworld stops for a moment. **Sisyphus** and **Tantalus** forget their torture. The , goddesses of vengeance, shed tears. [[Erinyes]]
In some versions, Orpheus touches Persephone, reminding her of his own kidnapping by Hades. The Queen of the Dead recognizes her pain.
Hades accepts the impossible: Eurydice can go back up. But an absolute condition. Orpheus must walk in front of her without turning around until they reach the light.
The climb back up is an ordeal. Behind him, silence. The shadows make no noise. Near the exit, doubt prevails. What if Hades had cheated on him? Orphée **turns around**.
Their eyes meet for a second. Then Eurydice is overcome by darkness. This time, the loss came from human error. The passage closes. Orpheus wanders, then retires to Thrace.

After his death, Orpheus' head, thrown into the  river, is said to have drifted to Lesbos. There she would have become an oracle, so powerful that **Apollo** himself would have demanded her silence. [[Hebros]]

His refusal of any new love provokes the fury of the , priestesses of **Dionysus** seized by a ritual delirium. They tear it apart. His lyre, however, continues to sing, carried away by the current. [[Maenads]]

From the death of Orpheus was born the , a religious movement which promised salvation for the soul through purification rites. Death is no longer a dreary end, but a passage to prepare for. [[Orphism]]

The “Orpheus gaze” still inspires opera, cinema, notably at , and literature. For , the artist is the one who looks into the darkness, even at the cost of losing what he loves. The gods finally place the lyre in the sky, in a constellation: the art lasts longer than the artist. [[Jean Cocteau]] [[Maurice Blanchot]]
**Orpheus** charms the Underworld with his music, then loses **Eurydice** by turning around too soon. Art can bend death; human doubt has the last word.
